title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: users can upload local and OneDrive files to custom engine agents
summary: The briefing accurately separates the planned upload capability from today's documented agent controls and limitations. The general metered-billing paragraph should also acknowledge Microsoft's documented exemption for qualifying Microsoft 365 Copilot licence holders.

claims.quote: Users will be able to upload files stored locally or in one drive to custom engine agents.

claims.claim: The planned upload also accepts files stored in OneDrive.

claims.claim: Custom engine agents bring their own orchestrator rather than using Copilot's.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Known issues currently lists file attachments as unsupported in custom engine agent chats.
claims.quote: Custom engine agents don't support file or image attachments in agent chats.

claims.claim: Images uploaded in chat are not passed to the agent for processing.
claims.quote: Images uploaded in chat aren't passed to the agent for processing.

claims.claim: The known-issues limitations apply to custom engine agents built with the Agents Toolkit and Agents SDK.

claims.claim: The known-issues page does not mention the planned upload change.
claims.quote: Searched: "custom engine agents" "file upload". Opened and read Known issues in full; its File attachments row states the current limitation and contains no announcement of local-or-OneDrive upload support.

claims.claim: The comparison table lists custom engine hosting in Microsoft 365 with Copilot Studio or externally with solutions such as Azure AI.
claims.quote: Hosted in Microsoft 365 with Copilot Studio or externally with custom solutions such as Azure AI.

claims.claim: The comparison table says custom engine builders must ensure their own compliance, responsible AI practices and security.
claims.quote: Must ensure your own compliance, RAI practices, and security measures.

claims.claim: The admin guide gives conflicting general guidance that both approaches adhere to Microsoft 365 security, compliance and responsible AI requirements.
claims.quote: Because both approaches use Copilot's AI infrastructure, model, and orchestrator, they adhere to the security, compliance, and Responsible AI (RAI) requirements for Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: An administrator reaches agent blocking through Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > All agents > agent > Block.
claims.quote: Select Agents > All agents. ... select an agent from the list of agents. ... immediately under the agent's name, select Block or Unblock.

claims.claim: The documented block API is beta.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not support production application use of the beta API.
claims.quote: Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: Block restricts access to the selected agent across the organisation.
claims.quote: These actions apply to the selected agent. ... Restrict access to an agent across the organization, preventing any user from using it.

claims.claim: For SharePoint- or Microsoft Foundry-created agents, blocking only affects availability in Microsoft Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: However, blocking an agent that you created by using SharePoint or Microsoft Foundry only impacts its availability in Microsoft Copilot Chat.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: The User access path is Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Settings > User access.
claims.quote: Select Agents > Settings > User access to manage your organization's agents and plugins.

claims.where: controls[1].scope; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: User access governs users' and groups' access to agents and plugins tenant-wide, not a selected agent.
claims.quote: Select who can access agents and plugins within your organization. ... Select Save to update your Copilot agent and plugin settings for your tenant.

claims.claim: All users is the default User access option.
claims.quote: All users - This option is the default. It means that all users in the organization can access agents and plugins, subject to the existing app policies and user assignments.

claims.claim: User access offers a No users option.
claims.quote: No users - This option means that no users in the organization can access agents and plugins.

claims.claim: User access offers a Specific users or groups option.
claims.quote: Specific users or groups - This option lets you select specific users or groups in your organization to have access to agents and plugins.

claims.claim: No automation equivalent for the tenant-wide User access setting is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph Copilot admin settings user access agents plugins specific users groups API; site:learn.microsoft.com/graph/api copilot admin settings user access agents plugins. Read Agent settings and Package Management API overview; no equivalent found.
